newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Shell says no bid plans for Woodside.
newsitem.headline: Shell says no bid plans for Woodside.

text.p: Shell Australia Ltd, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, on Wednesday denied share market rumours the group would make a bid for the shares in Australia's Woodside Petroleum Ltd it did not already own.
"The rumours were not true," a Shell Australia spokeswoman said.
Shell owns 34.3 percent of Woodside's 666.67 million issued shares and is a joint venture partner with it in the huge North West Shelf gas/condensate project offshore Western Australia.
"We have heard of that unofficial rumour, but we don't think there is much substance in it," said a spokesman for Woodside.
The rumours started when Woodside shares hit a record high of A$10.90 earlier today. The stock closed 23 cents or 2.17 percent up at A$10.82 on turnover of 1.34 million shares.
Oil and gas analysts also discounted the rumour pointing out that Woodside shares have doubled over the past year and if the Ango-Dutch oil giant was to make a bid it would have made it last year.
Analysts said Woodside received a mild boost to its shares today when it was awarded new exploration permits offshore Western Australia by the Australian government.
